plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: A fragrant evergreen shrub with silvery-green narrow leaves and dense spikes of small tubular flowers. It is widely cultivated for its essential oils, as an ornamental, and as a magnet for bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (June to August in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: Lavender fields in Provence typically reach peak bloom around early-to-mid July, and the name derives from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a large flower head made up of hundreds of tiny florets surrounded by bright yellow ray petals. The heads track the sun when young, a behavior called heliotropism.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall (July to September)
plants.location: Native to North America; widely grown in the United States, Ukraine, Russia, France, and Argentina
plants.funFact: The spiral arrangement of seeds in a sunflower head follows Fibonacci numbers, which allows optimal seed packing.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large round leaves held above the water and spectacular fragrant flowers on tall stalks. The leaves have a microscopic texture that makes water bead and roll off, carrying dirt away.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer (June to September in temperate Asia)
plants.location: Asia, from India and China to Japan and northern Australia; cultivated in ponds worldwide
plants.funFact: Lotus seeds have been germinated after more than 1,000 years of dormancy, and the flowers can regulate their own temperature to around 30-35°C.

plants.name: Telopea speciosissima
plants.description: A striking shrub with a large crimson flower head made of many small flowers surrounded by showy red bracts. It grows in the sandy, nutrient-poor soils of the sandstone country around Sydney.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere (August to November), with early flowers sometimes appearing in July
plants.funFact: It is the floral emblem of New South Wales, and its name 'Telopea' comes from the Greek for 'seen from afar'.
